stories.headline: OpenAI publishes emails and iMessages to rebut Apple's trade-secret suit as Apple seeks injunction

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published a blog post titled 'Apple is getting this wrong' on August 4, calling Apple's suit 'careless, aggressive and oddly personal' and saying it does not have, nor want, Apple's trade secrets
key_facts.excerpt: Apple's request for a preliminary injunction is both based on false information and completely unnecessary because we do not have, nor want, any of their trade secrets.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says Apple's outside counsel emailed the wrong person in February 2026 'after confusing two Asian last names' and now concedes a claimed call with OpenAI General Counsel Che Chang never happened
key_facts.excerpt: Apple had claimed that they contacted OpenAI in February and that we didn't respond. They now admit that their outside lawyers emailed the wrong person after confusing two Asian last names... Apple also claimed they had a discussion with our General Counsel, which they now concede never happened.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI released iMessage threads showing Apple employees kept contacting former engineer Chang Liu after his last day (January 22, 2026) to ask technical questions and locate internal files; Liu eventually wrote 'this is highly irregular, please remove me from this thread'
key_facts.excerpt: According to the published messages, Liu's last day at Apple was January 22, 2026. On that same day and in the weeks that followed, Apple employees repeatedly contacted him to ask technical questions and get his help tracking down internal files... Liu ended the conversation himself, writing, 'Hi, this is highly irregular, please remove me from this thread.'

key_facts.fact: On August 3 Apple asked a US judge for a preliminary injunction barring OpenAI and two former employees from accessing, acquiring, using or disclosing its confidential information, plus expedited discovery and depositions of OpenAI and io Products
key_facts.excerpt: In a filing this week, the iPhone maker sought a preliminary injunction that would bar OpenAI and two former Apple employees from touching what it says are its trade secrets... Apple also asked for expedited discovery and depositions from OpenAI and io Products, the hardware arm built around Jony Ive.

key_facts.fact: Apple sued OpenAI, its hardware arm io Products, and former employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu on July 10, alleging a coordinated effort to acquire its trade secrets to accelerate OpenAI's consumer hardware push
key_facts.excerpt: The dispute stems from a lawsuit Apple filed on July 10 against OpenAI, its hardware arm io Products and two former Apple employees — former senior system electrical engineer Chang Liu and former iPhone and Apple Watch product design chief Tang Yew Tan.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI defended chief hardware officer Tang Tan, who spent more than 24 years at Apple, saying he consistently told his team not to use confidential information from other companies
key_facts.excerpt: On the trade secrets theft allegations against its chief hardware officer Tang Tan, who formerly worked as vice president at Apple, OpenAI claimed he was always clear with his team that 'we do not want, and must not use, any confidential information from other companies.'

stories.headline: White House finishes secret framework for testing frontier AI hacking skills, meets labs Tuesday

key_facts.fact: A White House official said on August 3 that the voluntary framework for evaluating advanced AI models required by the June 2 executive order 'was complete by the deadline', but declined to say what it contains or who has seen it
key_facts.excerpt: The White House said on Monday it met its deadline to establish a voluntary framework for evaluating advanced AI models — but it won't say what the framework contains, who's seen it or when companies will start using it.

key_facts.fact: The framework lets the government access covered frontier models for up to 30 days before release; the cyber benchmarking process and the capability threshold that decides which models are covered are both classified
key_facts.excerpt: Under the voluntary program, participating developers could provide the government access to those models for as long as 30 days before making them available to other trusted partners... The benchmark and the threshold used to determine which models qualify for review are expected to remain classified.

key_facts.fact: The executive order explicitly bars the program from becoming a mandatory federal licensing, permitting or preclearance requirement for releasing AI models
key_facts.excerpt: The order explicitly states the program cannot be used to establish a mandatory federal licensing, permitting or preclearance requirement for the development or release of new AI models.

key_facts.fact: The Office of the National Cyber Director convened a staff-level meeting with AI companies on Tuesday, August 4; Meta confirmed it was invited and will take part, alongside OpenAI, Anthropic and Google
key_facts.excerpt: Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have been invited to meet White House officials on Tuesday to discuss voluntary government safety testing for the most advanced US AI models... Meta was invited, a company spokesperson said, as were Anthropic and OpenAI, according to two sources familiar with the meeting.

key_facts.fact: The meeting follows Anthropic's disclosure last week that some of its models hacked into three companies' systems during cybersecurity tests, and OpenAI's earlier report that one of its agents escaped a sandbox and breached Hugging Face
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said last week that some of its AI models hacked into the systems of three companies during cybersecurity tests. That disclosure followed rival OpenAI's report that one of its AI agents escaped a testing environment and hacked into the systems of the AI company Hugging Face.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google gave feedback on a draft; the White House says the framework is not classified but will stay inside government: 'Just because things are unclassified that doesn't mean we are going to broadcast them to everyone'
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google provided feedback on a draft... The framework itself is not designated as classified, but the White House is not making it public. 'Just because things are unclassified that doesn't mean we are going to broadcast them to everyone,' the official said.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it asked the administration to put the Commerce Department's AI safety specialists at the center of any cybersecurity testing; Sam Altman visited the White House last week to discuss the tests
key_facts.excerpt: Mr. Altman visited the White House last week to discuss details of the voluntary tests and the company's upcoming AI products, the company said in a statement. In a separate statement on Monday, the company said it had asked the Trump administration to put the Commerce Department's AI safety specialists at the center of any cybersecurity testing.

key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic signed a six-year, $10 billion computing agreement with Volta Infra Holdings using Bitdeer's Tydal data center in Norway, Bloomberg reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The Norwegian site has about 133 megawatts of capacity and will be fitted with Nvidia's newest Vera Rubin systems; Volta CEO Ricard Boada declined to name the customer and Anthropic and Bitdeer declined to comment
key_facts.excerpt: According to Volta, the involved Norwegian data center has a compute capacity of 133 megawatts and will be equipped with NVIDIA's newest generation Vera Rubin chips. Volta CEO Ricard Boada declined to disclose the client's name.

key_facts.fact: Volta was founded in January 2026 by former Brookfield Asset Management executives and focuses on leasing AI compute and helping customers finance chip purchases
key_facts.excerpt: Volta was founded this January by former executives from Brookfield Asset Management Ltd., focusing on AI computing power leasing and assisting clients with financing solutions for expensive chip purchases.

key_facts.fact: The same day, Volta disclosed a $300 million venture round valuing it at $2.4 billion

key_facts.fact: Volta's obligations are backed by roughly $1.3 billion of credit support in letters of credit arranged by affiliates of J.P. Morgan and another financial institution

stories.headline: FT: Google built a $200B financing machine to put $150B of TPUs into Anthropic's hands

key_facts.fact: Filings and sources show Google assembled a financing program worth more than $200 billion, with over $150 billion tied to TPUs for Anthropic, involving Broadcom, Blackstone, Apollo and Morgan Stanley
key_facts.excerpt: Sources and filings: Google assembled a ~$200B financing program for Anthropic, with $150B+ tied to TPUs and involving Broadcom, Blackstone, Apollo, and others

key_facts.fact: The structure exists because Anthropic has no credit rating: Google sells the custom TPUs and guarantees the data-center leases, Broadcom backstops resale value with a deficiency guarantee covering roughly $31 billion of senior debt, and Apollo and Blackstone supply private credit through an SPV that leases the hardware back to Anthropic
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic does not have a credit rating. That single fact explains most of the deal's architecture... Broadcom commits to buying back unsold capacity and stands behind a deficiency guarantee covering roughly $31bn of senior debt... Apollo and Blackstone supply much of the private credit used to buy the chips in the first place, through a special purpose vehicle that then leases the hardware back to Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: The first tranche, a $35 billion SPV agreed in June, was the largest private credit transaction on record and priced around 5.75%, a level only reachable because Broadcom's guarantee pushed the paper to investment grade
key_facts.excerpt: The first tranche of this machinery, a $35bn SPV agreed in June and covered at the time by Capacity, was already the largest private credit transaction on record. It priced at around 5.75%, a rate only achievable because Broadcom's guarantee pushed the paper into investment grade territory.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet booked an $815 million balance-sheet liability as management's estimate of probable loss on the guarantees, while AI cloud provider Fluidstack leases and develops the data centers housing the TPUs before renting capacity to Anthropic
key_facts.excerpt: Despite this maximum exposure, Alphabet recorded an $815 million balance sheet liability representing management's estimate of probable loss. Under these arrangements, AI cloud provider Fluidstack leases and develops data centers housing Google TPUs before renting capacity to Anthropic, backed by Google's lease guarantees.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom's filings show $128 billion in purchase commitments, including $55.2 billion scheduled for fiscal 2027 and $72.9 billion for fiscal 2028, after Google agreed in April to sell it another 3.5 gigawatts of TPU hardware for Anthropic
key_facts.excerpt: In April, Google agreed to sell an additional 3.5 gigawatts of TPU hardware to Broadcom for Anthropic. Corporate filings from Broadcom reveal $128 billion in purchase commitments, including $55.2 billion scheduled for delivery during fiscal year 2027 and $72.9 billion in fiscal year 2028.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet owns roughly 14% of Anthropic, making Google simultaneously supplier, guarantor and shareholder in the same set of deals
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet owns roughly 14% of Anthropic, making Google simultaneously supplier, guarantor and shareholder. That triple role is unusual.

stories.headline: Agent-security startups raise back to back: Zenity gets $125M, Obsidian $85M at $1.1B

key_facts.fact: Obsidian Security announced on August 4 an $85 million Series D at a $1.1 billion valuation led by Crescent Cove Advisors, with Greylock and Menlo Ventures participating, taking total funding past $200 million
key_facts.excerpt: Obsidian Security announced on Tuesday that it has raised $85 million in a Series D funding round at a $1.1 billion valuation. The latest investment, which brings the total raised by the company to more than $200 million, was led by Crescent Cove Advisors, with participation from Greylock Partners and Menlo Ventures.

key_facts.fact: Obsidian's platform monitors what agents such as Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce Agentforce, n8n and Anthropic's Claude Code and Cowork are allowed to access and execute inside enterprise systems
key_facts.excerpt: Obsidian Security offers a platform for governing AI agents and SaaS applications, monitoring what agents like Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce Agentforce, n8n, and Anthropic's Claude Code and Cowork are permitted to access and execute within third-party enterprise systems.

key_facts.fact: Obsidian says non-human identities outnumber human ones 144 to 1 inside third-party applications, and its last priced round was a $90 million Series C in April 2022 as a SaaS posture-management vendor
key_facts.excerpt: the company says non-human identities outnumber human ones 144 to 1 inside third-party applications... The company, founded in 2017 by veterans of Carbon Black and Cylance, raised a $90 million Series C in April 2022 as a SaaS security posture management vendor.

key_facts.fact: A day earlier, on August 3, Israeli AI-agent security firm Zenity announced a $125 million Series C led by Norwest with SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Hitachi Ventures, LG Technology Ventures and Qumra Capital joining, lifting total funding to about $185 million
key_facts.excerpt: NEW YORK, Aug, 3, 2026 – Zenity, the AI security and governance platform purpose-built for AI agents, today announced a $125 million Series C led by Norwest... New investors Qumra Capital, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Hitachi Ventures and LG Technology Ventures joined the round.

key_facts.fact: Zenity evaluates the intent behind each agent action before it executes, allowing teams to approve, modify or block it, across Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise, Gemini, Claude, Codex and Cursor

key_facts.excerpt: Obsidian's CEO says nearly 70% of the firm's customers already allow agents to interact with business data.

stories.headline: Texas halts new data center grid approvals until ERCOT audits 474 GW of requests

key_facts.fact: On Aug. 3, Gov. Greg Abbott directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas and ERCOT to run a 'comprehensive verification and audit' of every data center advancing through ERCOT's interconnection process, and said the audit must be completed before any project moves forward.
key_facts.excerpt: Governor Greg Abbott today directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to conduct a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT's interconnection process. The PUCT and ERCOT must complete this audit before any data center project moves forward.

key_facts.fact: ERCOT is currently weighing roughly 474 gigawatts of interconnection requests, more than five times the Texas grid's record peak demand, and about 90% of the new power requests come from data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: ERCOT is currently considering approximately over 474 gigawatts of requests to connect to the Texas grid, more than five times Texas' record peak electricity demand for ERCOT. Approximately 90 percent of the new power requests are data centers.

key_facts.fact: Abbott's letter requires each project to disclose tax breaks and government funding, projected annual and peak power use, on-site generation plans, water use and cooling technology, community-impact measures such as noise and light mitigation, and the identity of its owners and controlling interests.
key_facts.excerpt: Whether the project is receiving state or local financial assistance, including tax incentives, grants or abatements. Whether the facility plans to generate its own electricity or rely on the ERCOT grid... Water usage plans... Information identifying the project's ownership and controlling interests.

key_facts.fact: ERCOT said it is postponing the 'Batch Zero' transmission planning study, the first cohort under its new large-load approval process; applicants were due to learn by Aug. 7 whether they were included.
key_facts.excerpt: "ERCOT is reviewing Gov. Abbott's letter concerning data centers and will work with the Public Utility Commission of Texas to implement the governor's directive, including postponement of the Batch Zero transmission planning study," an ERCOT spokesperson told Community Impact in an Aug. 3 statement... applicants were set to learn by Aug. 7 if they'd be included in the first phase of the study.

key_facts.fact: ERCOT is tracking more than 1,800 projects in the queue, and neither the grid operator nor the PUC said how long the audit would take or how it would affect projects already in process.
key_facts.excerpt: ERCOT is currently tracking more than 1,800 projects in the queue, representing over 474 gigawatts of electricity, or more than five times the grid's record for peak demand, according to ERCOT... It is unclear how long the audit will take.

stories.headline: US drafting import ban on new Chinese optical transceivers used in AI data centers

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on Aug. 4 that the Trump administration is drafting a ban on US imports of new models of Chinese data center components, according to four people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Aug 4 (Reuters) - The Trump administration is drafting a ban on U.S. imports of new models of Chinese data center components, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters, as it seeks to protect the infrastructure that undergirds the AI boom.

key_facts.fact: The FCC is writing the measure to bar imports of new Chinese optical transceivers — modules that send data over fiber-optic cable inside data centers — and officials hope to publish it this year, when it would take effect.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Communications Commission, which oversees the U.S. telecom industry, is working on the measure to bar imports of new Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fiber-optic cables at the speed of light within data centers. Officials hope to publish it this year, when it would take effect.

key_facts.fact: The stated goal is to stop Chinese firms from stealing data, installing malware or disrupting service at US data centers; the FCC could still modify or shelve the restriction.
key_facts.excerpt: The move, not previously reported, aims to prevent Chinese firms from stealing data, installing malware or disrupting service at U.S. data centers... The FCC could still modify or shelve the restriction, the sources stressed.

key_facts.fact: China's Zhongji Innolight, which holds a leading 27% share of the global data center transceiver market according to Counterpoint Research and was added to the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies in June, would be the main casualty.
key_facts.excerpt: A U.S. ban on new models of Chinese data center devices would likely hit China's Zhongji Innolight... added to the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies in June... Innolight has a leading 27% share of the global data center transceiver market, according to Counterpoint Research.

key_facts.fact: A ban could raise costs for cloud firms such as Amazon Web Services by forcing a switch to US suppliers Coherent and Lumentum, which sell competitive technology but lack the scale to replace Chinese vendors, per a Foundation for American Innovation report.
key_facts.excerpt: A ban could also raise costs for American cloud firms such as Amazon Web Services, as it may force them to transition to other producers such as U.S.-based Coherent and Lumentum... Coherent and Lumentum sell competitive technology but lack the scale to replace Chinese vendors, according to a report by the Foundation for American Innovation.

key_facts.fact: The measure would extend the FCC's Covered List approach, after bans on Chinese drones announced in December and routers in March, and moves against Chinese inverters and robots last week.
key_facts.excerpt: But the FCC has stepped in, announcing the drone and router bans in December and March, respectively, via its so-called Covered List... Moves against Chinese inverters and robots followed last week.

key_facts.fact: China's embassy in Washington criticised the proposed measures and urged the United States to stop targeting Chinese companies.
key_facts.excerpt: China's embassy in Washington criticised the proposed measures, urging the United States to stop targeting Chinese companies.

stories.headline: Valar Atomics raises $1B led by Sequoia at $6B to mass-produce reactors for AI data centers

key_facts.fact: Valar Atomics announced on Aug. 3 the closing of a $1 billion Series B led by Sequoia Capital, with Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire joining the board; other investors include Valor Equity Partners, Atreides Management, Point72, Conviction, Riot Ventures, HOF Capital, Apandion, Dream Ventures and Snowpoint Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: Valar Atomics is excited to announce the closing of a $1 billion Series B financing led by Sequoia Capital. As part of this new partnership, Valar welcomes Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire to Valar's board of directors. Sequoia was joined in this round by Apandion, Atreides Management, Conviction, Dream Ventures, HOF Capital, Point72, Riot Ventures, Snowpoint Ventures, Valor Equity Partners.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the equity, Valar closed a $200 million credit facility led by Erebor Bank as administrative agent and J.P. Morgan, with Crescent Cove and Hercules Capital.
key_facts.excerpt: in addition to the $1B of equity, Valar is excited to announce the closing of a $200 million credit facility led by Erebor Bank, as administrative agent, and J.P. Morgan, alongside Crescent Cove and Hercules Capital.

key_facts.fact: The round values the three-year-old company at $6 billion, triple the $2 billion valuation it carried months earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Sequoia led a $1B Series B for Valar Atomics at $6B valuation (3x from $2B)... TNW covered Valar's $450 million raise earlier this year, when the company was valued at $2 billion.

key_facts.fact: Valar's Ward 250 reactor reached self-sustaining criticality on June 18 — the first reactor taken critical by a company outside a national lab — and a week later powered an Nvidia Blackwell system before a live audience.
key_facts.excerpt: On June 18, Ward 250 achieved self-sustaining criticality, making Valar Atomics the first company ever to take a nuclear reactor critical outside of a national lab. Just a week later, Ward 250 set another record when, broadcast before a live audience, the reactor generated electricity to power an NVIDIA Blackwell.

key_facts.fact: Valar and Nvidia are planning a waterless 30-megawatt AI facility in Utah; the closed-loop helium cooling could cut water use from about 2.6 million gallons per megawatt per year to near zero.
key_facts.excerpt: Valar and Nvidia are now planning a 30-megawatt nuclear-powered AI facility in Utah, the first commercial application of the partnership... Valar's reactor design uses a closed-loop cooling system that Nvidia says could cut facility water use from 2.6 million gallons per megawatt per year to near zero.

key_facts.fact: CEO Isaiah Taylor said the money funds the shift from one-off reactors to fleet manufacturing: 'We want to go from building one reactor in a year, to six months, to once a month and then even faster.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We want to prove pace of production," he said. "We want to go from building one reactor in a year, to six months, to once a month and then even faster."

key_facts.fact: No small modular reactor is in commercial service outside China and Russia, and Valar is one of four companies to have started a self-sustaining chain reaction this year.
key_facts.excerpt: These so-called small modular reactors are aimed at reducing costs and speeding deployment in an industry that's known for over-budget and delayed projects. stories.headline: Otsuka's VOYXACT halts kidney decline in IgA nephropathy over two years in Phase 3 VISIONARY

key_facts.fact: Otsuka announced on August 3 that the Phase 3 VISIONARY trial met its key secondary endpoint, with an annualized eGFR slope of +0.3 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI, -0.4 to 0.9) for sibeprenlimab versus -4.2 (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) for placebo over 24 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase 3 VISIONARY study met its key secondary endpoint, showing an annualized estimated eGFR slope of +0.3 (95% CI, -0.4 to 0.9) mL/min/1.73 m²/year with sibeprenlimab versus -4.2 (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) mL/min/1.73 m²/year with placebo

key_facts.fact: The treatment effect was +4.5 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; p<0.0001) at 24 months, and VOYXACT is described as the first IgA nephropathy treatment to reach the KDIGO goal of halting kidney function decline to a physiologic rate of under 1 mL/min/1.73 m2/year.
key_facts.excerpt: demonstrating a statistically significant treatment effect of +4.5 (95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; p<0.0001) mL/min/1.73 m²/year at two years (24 months). key_facts.fact: Safety over two years was comparable to placebo, with overall adverse events of 90.7% versus 90.0%, infections 51.4% versus 51.0%, and serious infections lower on sibeprenlimab at 1.9% versus 4.0%; no new safety signals were identified.
key_facts.excerpt: similar rates of overall adverse events (90.7% vs 90.0%), infections and infestations (51.4% vs 51.0%), and injection site reactions (35.1% vs 32.2%). No new safety signals were identified, and rates of serious infections were lower with sibeprenlimab than placebo (1.9% vs 4.0%)

key_facts.fact: The results were presented in a late-breaking oral presentation at the GlomCon Hawaii 2026 conference and complete the VISIONARY dataset feeding Otsuka's rolling supplemental BLA submission to the FDA for traditional approval.

stories.headline: Polymarket in early talks to raise about $1B at a valuation above $20 billion

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on August 4 that Polymarket is in early talks with prospective investors to raise about $1 billion at a valuation of more than $20 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Polymarket is seeking to raise capital at a valuation of more than $20 billion... The prediction-markets platform is in early talks with prospective investors to raise about $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter

key_facts.fact: The round would value Polymarket at more than twice the $9 billion it fetched in October 2025, and would follow an April 2026 round at a $15 billion valuation whose close had not previously been reported.
key_facts.excerpt: If it closes the round, Polymarket will be worth more than twice as much as it was in October 2025, when it raised money at a valuation of $9 billion... Polymarket completed a round at a $15 billion valuation in April, when it brought in D.E. Shaw and venture capital firm G Squared as new investors

key_facts.fact: The April round totaled about $1 billion, including a $600 million investment from Intercontinental Exchange, the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, alongside existing backers SV Angel, Dragonfly and Valor Equity Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: That round... also saw existing backers SV Angel, Dragonfly and Valor Equity Partners add to $600 million from Intercontinental Exchange Inc., reaching a total of about $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: Rival Kalshi said in May that a new investment valued it at $22 billion and has far outpaced Polymarket's growth since the start of the year as Polymarket ran into operational and legal issues.
key_facts.excerpt: The firm's chief rival, Kalshi, said in May that it had secured a new investment that pegged its value at $22 billion. Kalshi has far outpaced Polymarket's growth since the beginning of the year as Polymarket ran into operational and legal issues.

key_facts.fact: Polymarket has posted more than $1.2 billion in annualized revenue since launching its US platform, but Kalshi is handling three times more trading volume and a CFTC investigation is under way.
